assumptions: No historical actuals are available for this project; estimate is based on story points and task complexity only.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 effective hours of blended work, scaled up for integration/coordination overhead on complex tasks (RBAC, payments, migration).

Backend Developer FTE = 1.5 people ≈ 120 hrs/week capacity; Frontend = 1.0 FTE ≈ 80 hrs/week; QA = 0.6 FTE ≈ 48 hrs/week; DevOps = 0.4 FTE ≈ 32 hrs/week - all roles are staffed thinly relative to backlog, implying a multi-sprint (roughly 10-12 week) delivery timeline rather than a short burst.
DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) is the tightest constraint and is only allocated to CI/pipeline, migration infra, and payment webhook infra work - not general support.
QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) effort is concentrated on the urgent/high priority items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration) with lighter coverage on medium priority items.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is treated as high-risk and includes extra Backend + QA + DevOps time for validation/reconciliation given the volume (400k customers, 2M invoice lines).
Payment provider integration (PW-7) includes webhook handling and reconciliation logic, requiring both Backend and QA time plus DevOps for secure webhook infra.
Design system (PW-2) is primarily Frontend-led with minimal QA/Backend involvement.
Estimate excludes ongoing post-launch support/maintenance costs - scope is limited to delivering the 8 backlog items to production-ready state.
A ~12% contingency is implicitly reflected in the P80 scenario to account for estimation uncertainty given lack of actuals.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox & test transaction costs
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / temporary read-replica licensing
Design system asset licensing (icons, theming tokens)

input.reasoning: Effort was sized per backlog item using story points as a relative complexity proxy, translated into role-specific hours based on the nature of each task (e.g., CI/pipeline skews DevOps+Backend, design system skews Frontend, RBAC/payments/migration skew Backend+QA+DevOps). Hours were then checked against each role's FTE capacity to confirm the allocation is plausible over a ~10-12 week delivery window rather than an unrealistic compressed sprint. Backend Developer carries the largest share of hours given RBAC, payments, dashboard, invoice view, and migration all require significant API/service work. QA hours are concentrated on urgent/high risk items. DevOps hours are deliberately capped given only 0.4 FTE is available, limited to CI setup, migration infra, and payment webhook security. Non-labour costs cover third-party tooling (Stripe, cloud hosting, migration tooling, design assets) that are typically billed separately from labour. Total labour cost of ~$131,264.60 plus ~$5,900 non-labour gives a base (P50) estimate of ~$137,165, with P80/P90 scenarios adding contingency for the acknowledged estimation uncertainty (no historical actuals, high complexity of migration and payments).

reductions.description: Defer Design system and component library (PW-2, Medium priority) to a post-launch phase and use a base Angular Material theme initially instead of a fully custom component library.
reductions.effect: Removes most Frontend hours allocated to PW-2 (~165 hrs) and associated design asset licensing; delays polish but not core functionality.

reductions.description: Reduce QA coverage on Medium priority items (PW-2, PW-6) to smoke testing only rather than full test cycles, relying on developer self-testing.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~60 QA hours from lower-risk backlog items while retaining full QA rigor on Urgent/High items.

reductions.description: Descope PDF download from Invoice list and detail view (PW-6) to a follow-up release, delivering only the paged list and detail view initially.
reductions.effect: Removes Backend and Frontend hours tied to PDF generation/rendering (~35 hrs combined).

reductions.description: Use a managed migration service/off-the-shelf ETL tool instead of custom-built migration scripts for PW-8, reducing Backend engineering hours.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~70 Backend hours and ~10 DevOps hours on PW-8 by leveraging existing tooling instead of fully bespoke code, offset partially by tooling licensing already included in non-labour.

reductions.description: Delay non-critical staging environment hardening and use a minimal single-environment CI setup for initial launch.
reductions.effect: Reduces DevOps hours on PW-1 by ~8 hrs and cloud hosting non-labour spend.
